purpose: Fresh synthetic source-fidelity holdout for the revised production judge; not title generation, not a new-channel end-to-end test.

holdoutProtocol.designBasis: Only previously reported failure classes: figurative phrasing misread as literal invention, insufficient evidence misread as contradiction, and a compatible plain title rejected for not being the most theatrical option.
holdoutProtocol.sealScope: Freeze fixture bytes and hashes before the revised prompt is inspected or this holdout is replayed. Any later revision requires a new reported version, not silent correction after results.
holdoutProtocol.doNotLeak: Do not give sources, titles, labels or rationales to the prompt editor until the parent has recorded the revised prompt freeze.

policy.judgeInputAllowlist: Send only inputs[i].args and inputs[i].candidates to judgeTitleCandidates. Never send IDs, provenance, expectations, purpose or this holdout protocol.
policy.labelsAre: Human-designed holdout expectations, not model output, owner approval or creative generation answers.
policy.notGenerationExamples: Never use these candidates as production titles, prompt hints, few-shot examples or substitute outputs in an automatic new-channel test.
policy.candidateOrder: Three supported-first and three unsupported-first pairs; original and reversed replay must remap indexes before comparison.
policy.scope: English source fidelity and channel compatibility only. No measured creativity, virality, multilingual, rendered-video or pipeline-quality claim.

hashConventions.sourceTextSha256: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 inputs[].args.scriptExcerpt, without normalization

args.topic: Reading seasonal layers in a sampled glacier core
args.persona: A measured field-science narrator making physical evidence understandable without inflating what a sample proves. Vivid accessible language is welcome; the explanation stays specific to the observation.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic field record: The team examined an ice core containing 37 consecutive annual layers. Each layer represents snowfall from one winter, and the trapped dust lets the episode compare conditions across those 37 winters. The glacier's surveyed edge is 370 metres wide; that measurement is a width, not the age or layer count of the core. The episode reconstructs the changing conditions recorded in the sampled layers.

args.topic: Dormancy and later germination in a common wildflower seed lot
args.persona: A patient, practical garden educator explaining why familiar living things behave unexpectedly. The voice is friendly and curious, with ordinary language rather than miracle claims.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic greenhouse record: A batch of living seeds from a common, abundant wildflower did not germinate during a dry storage period. They remained viable in dormancy. After the gardener supplied moisture and a suitable temperature, they germinated and grew into ordinary plants of that same species. The experiment demonstrates delayed germination in viable seeds; the species is not extinct and the seeds did not die during storage.

candidates.title: The Extinct Flower Brought Back From the Dead
The Seeds That Hit the Snooze Button

args.topic: Diagnosing and repairing a cello's unstable bridge
args.persona: A quiet, visually led craft storyteller who lets diagnosis and skilled repair carry the episode. Titles may be evocative or plain, but must promise the work and material story actually shown.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic workshop record: A student brought a cello to the repair bench because it produced a thin buzz instead of a clear note. The luthier found that the bridge had shifted and no longer supported the strings correctly. After resetting the bridge and checking the setup, the luthier played the same musical phrase again; the notes were clear and resonant. The episode follows the instrument's diagnosis, adjustment and sound comparison.

candidates.title: The Cello That Found Its Voice Again
The Lost Tape That Gave a Cellist Her Father Back

args.topic: A cache-key collision that returned incorrect search results
args.persona: An energetic but candid developer team explaining mistakes through concrete observations. The audience likes a human account of the investigation, with precise boundaries between incorrect results and lost data.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic team postmortem: We spent Saturday and Sunday tracking a search-results bug. Two different queries accidentally shared one cache key, so the second query could receive the first query's cached answer. The persistent search index and every customer's stored records remained unchanged. We fixed the cache-key construction and invalidated the incorrect cached answers. The episode traces the two-day investigation and the final correction.

candidates.title: The Cache Bug That Erased Every Customer's Data
The Cache Bug That Ate Our Weekend

args.topic: An unresolved investigation into a marsh fish die-off
args.persona: A clear local-science reporter who distinguishes observations from causal conclusions. Direct questions and useful explanations are both appropriate; uncertainty remains visible until the investigation resolves it.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic investigation record: Several fish were found dead in the marsh after heavy rain. Samples collected later showed low oxygen, but investigators could not determine whether oxygen had fallen before or after the fish died. A resident also reported possible pesticide runoff, but no retained sample established that pesticides reached the marsh. The report compares the two hypotheses. The available evidence does not establish the cause of the die-off.

candidates.title: Pesticides Caused the Marsh Fish Die-Off

args.topic: A forged nineteenth-century letter whose author remains unidentified
args.niche: fictional literary archives and document attribution
args.persona: A careful archive storyteller separating the physical authenticity of an object from uncertainty about its maker. A straightforward evidence-led title is welcome; atmosphere must not turn a known finding into a mystery or a mystery into certainty.
args.scriptExcerpt: Synthetic archive record: A letter offered as an 1842 original by the fictional poet Edda Voss was examined. Its paper contains a manufacturer's watermark first introduced in 1996. The catalogue review and material examination establish that this object is not an authentic 1842 letter. The investigation has not identified who made the forgery; competing attributions remain unresolved. The episode explains the physical proof of forgery and the still-open authorship question.

candidates.title: A Forged Letter and Its Unknown Author

candidates.reason: Diary personifies the physical record; it does not assert a literal book or a writing glacier. Thirty-seven winters follows the specified thirty-seven annual layers.

The core contains thirty-seven annual layers, not three hundred seventy. The latter number is the glacier edge's width, not recorded winters. Accepting the metaphor does not permit changing its quantity.
